statements.t: While memory chip pressures and customer deployment timing continue to impact near-term performance, we remain confident in the long-term demand for our products and opportunities to expand our portfolio.
Including our recently announced $1.50 per share special distribution, we will have distributed $16.50 per share in 2026.
Looking ahead, we are revising our full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $180 million to $200 million, primarily resulting from customer demand being pushed out into 2027.

We remain confident in the underlying demand for our products and are focused on managing costs, maintaining financial flexibility and positioning the business to capitalize on longer-term network upgrade opportunities," said Kyle Lorentzen, Chief Financial Officer.

Although the information contained in this press release represents our best judgment as of the date of this release based on information currently available and reasonable assumptions, we can give no assurance that the expectations will be attained or that any deviation will not be material.

statements.t: Following the divestiture of the Connectivity and Cable Solutions (CCS) segment that was completed on January 9, 2026, we initiated a new restructuring plan to right-size our cost structure and align operations with our revised business scope.

We expect to continue to incur such costs during the remainder of 2026 as we continue executing on our current transformation initiative, and the resulting charges and cash requirements could be material.

The net restructuring costs recorded in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were primarily related to our new restructuring plan to right-size our cost structure and align operations with our revised business scope.
We expect to make cash payments of $2.9 million in the remainder of 2026 and $1.5 million during 2027 to settle our restructuring actions.
Additional restructuring actions related to our restructuring efforts are expected to be identified, and the resulting charges and cash requirements could be material.
As a result, we expect to release a portion of our reserve for uncertain tax positions during the fourth quarter of 2026.

Although the information contained in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q represents our best judgment as of the date of this report based on information currently available and reasonable assumptions, we can give no assurance that the expectations will be attained or that any deviation will not be material.

estimates.t: There have been no changes in our critical accounting policies as disclosed in our 2025 Annual Report.

estimates.name: Net sales
estimates.t: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, net sales which were primarily attributable to Aurora, decreased by $18.1 million, or 5.4%, and increased $40.2 million, or 4.5%, respectively, compared to the prior year periods.

estimates.name: Gross profit, TSA income, SG&A expense and R&D expense — Gross profit (net sales less cost
estimates.t: Gross profit decreased by $8.0 million and $28.8 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the prior year periods.

estimates.name: Transition service agreement income
estimates.t: TSA income relates to agreements we entered into with Belden and Amphenol in connection with the divestitures of the RUCKUS segment, CCS segment, OWN segment and DAS business unit.

estimates.name: Selling, general and administrative expense
estimates.t: Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expense decreased by $26.2 million and $53.7 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the prior year periods.
estimates.effect: Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expense decreased by $26.2 million and $53.7 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the prior year periods.

estimates.name: Research and development expense
estimates.t: Research and development (R&D) expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 decreased by $15.2 million and $33.6 million, respectively, primarily due to lower variable incentive compensation, compared to the prior year periods.
estimates.effect: Research and development (R&D) expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 decreased by $15.2 million and $33.6 million, respectively, primarily due to lower variable incentive compensation, compared to the prior year periods.

estimates.name: Aurora and consolidated results
estimates.t: Reflects the results of Aurora, our reportable segment, which represent substantially all of our net sales and exclude general corporate costs that were previously allocated to the divested businesses because they were not directly attributable to the divested businesses.

estimates.name: Operating income and adjusted EBITDA
estimates.t: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, Aurora operating income decreased and Aurora adjusted EBITDA increased compared to the prior year period.
estimates.effect: Aurora operating income was also unfavorably impacted by an increase in equity-based compensation expense of $4.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 which is not reflected in adjusted EBITDA.

estimates.name: Amortization of purchased intangible assets and Restructuring costs, net — Amortization of
estimates.t: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, amortization of purchased intangible assets was lower compared to the prior year periods because certain of our intangible assets became fully amortized.

estimates.name: Restructuring costs, net
estimates.t: The net restructuring costs recorded in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were primarily related to our new restructuring plan to right-size our cost structure and align operations with our revised business scope.

estimates.name: Other income (expense), net — Foreign currency loss
estimates.t: Foreign currency loss includes the net foreign currency gains and losses resulting from the settlement of receivables and payables, foreign currency contracts and short-term intercompany advances in a currency other than the subsidiary’s functional currency.

estimates.name: Other income (expense), net
estimates.t: Other income (expense), net for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was favorably impacted by gains on certain financial assets.
estimates.effect: For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, other income (expense), net includes $1.1 million of debt issuance costs related to a debt refinancing transaction that occurred in the fourth quarter of 2024.

estimates.name: Interest expense, Interest income and Income taxes — Interest expense and Interest income
estimates.t: Upon completion of the sale of the CCS segment on January 9, 2026, we repaid our outstanding third‑party debt.

estimates.name: Income tax (expense) benefit
estimates.t: Our income taxes were less than the statutory rate of 21.0% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to $24.2 million and $24.7 million, respectively, of tax benefit associated with the release of certain uncertain tax positions.
estimates.effect: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, we recognized an income tax benefit of $20.0 million on pretax income of $34.7 million and an income tax benefit of $42.3 million on pretax income of $55.1 million, respectively.
